title: The Risk Practice

header.html: Explain the purpose of the risk practice and its relationships with the principles; explain the purpose of the risk management approach and the risk register; define risk, risk appetite, risk tolerance, risk cause, event and effect, risk exposure, risk owner, risk action owner, probability and impact; describe risk planning, analysis, control, culture, decision bias, the recommended response types and the use of data
the official PRINCE2 7 Foundation syllabus (PeopleCert), learning outcome 4.5

html:
1Purpose

The risk practice provides a structured way to identify, assess and manage the uncertainties that could affect the project's objectives, so that threats are reduced and opportunities are taken.

2Key concepts

Term Meaning
Risk A threat or opportunity based on uncertainty: something that might happen and would affect objectives
Risk appetite The amount of risk an organization is willing to take to reach its objectives
Risk tolerance The limit of risk exposure that is acceptable at a given level; beyond it, escalate
Risk exposure The extent to which the project is exposed to the risk's impact
Risk probability The chance that the risk will happen
Risk impact The effect on objectives if it does happen
Risk owner Accountable for managing the risk
Risk action owner Carries out an action to respond to the risk

Cause, event and effect

A risk is described in three parts: the cause (the situation), the event (what might happen) and the effect (what it would mean for objectives).

Exam tip

. Risk = uncertain (might happen). Issue = has already happened. Risk owner is accountable; action owner does the action. Appetite = willingness; tolerance = limit.

3Risk guidance

Guidance Meaning
Risk planning Agree the approach, roles and scales before the project starts to manage risk
Risk analysis Identify risks and assess their probability, impact and proximity (when)
Risk control Plan responses, implement them, monitor and communicate
Risk culture An open, honest environment where people raise risks without blame
Decision bias Unconscious tendencies (optimism, anchoring) that distort risk judgments; watch for them
Use of data Use data and tools to analyze and monitor risk

The risk technique has five steps: identify, assess, plan, implement, communicate. [Verify live]

Recommended response types

Type Responses
Threats Avoid, reduce, fallback, transfer, accept, share
Opportunities Exploit, enhance, share, reject

[Verify live] The wording of the response lists.

4Management products

Product Purpose
Risk management approach (PID) How risk is managed on this project: scales, roles, appetite and tolerance
Risk register (project log) A record of identified risks, their owners, assessment and responses
Exam tip

. A risk has a cause, event and effect. If a statement says something has happened, it is an issue, not a risk.

Exam tip

. Threat responses include avoid, reduce, fallback, transfer, accept, share; opportunity responses include exploit, enhance, share, reject. Share appears in both.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A supplier might deliver late, which would delay testing. Which term describes this?

  • AAn issue
  • BAn exception
  • CA risk
  • DA benefit
Show the answer

Answer: C. It might happen, so it is a risk; an issue has already happened.

S2Which statements are CORRECT? (1) A risk can be a threat or an opportunity. (2) A risk owner is accountable for managing the risk. (3) A risk action owner is accountable for the risk. (4) A risk is something that has already happened.

  • A3 and 4
  • B2 and 3
  • C1 and 2
  • D1 and 4
Show the answer

Answer: C. Risks are threats or opportunities, and the risk owner is accountable.

S3Identify the missing word. Risk [ ? ] is the amount of risk an organization is willing to take to reach its objectives.

  • AImpact
  • BExposure
  • CAppetite
  • DTolerance
Show the answer

Answer: C. That is risk appetite.

S4The team decides to buy insurance so another party bears the financial impact. Which threat response is this?

  • AAvoid
  • BAccept
  • CTransfer
  • DReduce
Show the answer

Answer: C. Moving the impact to another party is transfer.

S5The team chooses to exploit an opportunity. Which statement fits?

  • AIt tries to make the opportunity definitely happen
  • BIt ignores the opportunity
  • CIt makes a threat less likely
  • DIt records an issue
Show the answer

Answer: A. Exploit makes sure the opportunity is realized.

S6Where is the list of identified risks, owners and responses recorded?

  • AThe product register
  • BThe risk register
  • CThe highlight report
  • DThe work package description
Show the answer

Answer: B. The risk register records risks and responses.

5.2 Recall questions

R1Define a risk.

Show the answer

A threat or opportunity based on uncertainty.

R2What are the three parts of a risk description?

Show the answer

Cause, event and effect.

R3What is risk tolerance?

Show the answer

The limit of risk exposure acceptable at a given level.

R4Name the threat responses.

Show the answer

Avoid, reduce, fallback, transfer, accept and share.

R5Name the opportunity responses.

Show the answer

Exploit, enhance, share and reject.

R6Name the five steps of the risk technique.

Show the answer

Identify, assess, plan, implement and communicate.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Risk threat or opportunity from uncertainty (cause, event, effect)
Appetite / tolerance willingness / limit
Owners risk owner accountable; action owner acts
Threat responses avoid, reduce, fallback, transfer, accept, share
Opportunity responses exploit, enhance, share, reject
Products risk management approach, risk register
